42 CFR 456.705(b) requires point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review of drug therapy using predetermined standards before each prescription is filled or delivered, with screening for specified types of potential drug therapy problems [42-CFR-456.705(b)].

Screening must identify: (1) therapeutic duplication (two or more drugs from the same class such that the combined daily dose risks an adverse result or adds cost without added benefit); (2) drug-disease contraindication [42-CFR-456.705(b)(1)-(2)].

It must also identify: (3) adverse drug-drug interaction; (4) incorrect drug dosage (dosage outside the daily dosage in the predetermined standards; strength x quantity dispensed / day's supply); (5) incorrect duration of drug treatment; (6) drug-allergy interactions [42-CFR-456.705(b)(3)-(6)].
Seventh, screening must identify clinical abuse/misuse (situations covered by the definitions of abuse, gross overuse, overutilization) [42-CFR-456.705(b)(7)].

The review is conditioned on exceptions in 42 CFR 456.703(b) and (c), and companion retrospective DUR rules (456.709(b)) monitor many of the same problem types against the 456.705(b) definitions [42-CFR-456.705(b), 42-CFR-456.709(b)].
